sources: LP1 1:46:25-1:52:08 (archive.org PS4 longplay Part 1; 2 fps frames, HUD counter crops)

Nitro switch detonates all remaining Nitro and they are added to the count), switch (iron ! box, not counted), outline (wireframe crate materialised by a !), phase (translucent blue crate that is solid only in one Lani-Loli phase), phaseTnt, fire (dark crate with brass vents that jet flame; GR 'fire crate'), checkpoint (counted), aku, unknown (type not resolvable from frames). observations: There are no grind rails: the 'dragon' is a sweeping hazard and the linear structures are plank ledges, gold-band ledges and ropes.

Blue gem: finish without breaking any crate (checkpoints, TNT and Nitro included) - GR.

geometryObservations: The signature hazard is shown before it is dangerous. A spectral dragon flies over the garden path at 1:46:59-1:47:04 without touching Crash (O-S1-a), and the first dragon-swept wall comes about 1.5 minutes later (O-S4-b).

Floors and walls alternate. Every 2D climb starts from a wide floor that works as a perch (stair top, landing P-S4-c, floating courtyard P-S5-c), and most climbs end on a checkpoint floor (C2, C4, C6, C7).

Wall climbs use one shelf module of about 2 x 1 u, spaced 2-5 u apart. The first wall's shelves crumble, so the player must keep moving (P-S2-c, GP). The dragon wall's shelves are static but swept, so the player must wait (P-S4-d). The two rules never share a wall.

Gong monks follow teach, test, combine. The first monk is alone on a walkway backed by a wall (E-S2-a). The second sits over a 1-deep walkway (E-S3-a), then 3-4 monks fill a gallery the whirlwind crosses (E-S3-b), and the final gauntlet pairs bells side by side (E-S7-a, GP).

The mask sets the gap scale. Before Akano, gaps are 2-3 u (double-jump scale). Right after it, the level opens 5-6 u hover gaps (G-S4-b, bonus G-B-a), and the first floating crate after the pickup teaches the hover.
Guardian lions appear only at the ends of transitions and always on wide floors: the stair top, the archway, an alcove and the final court. They test the whirlwind attack, never the jump.
The secret is marked by an enemy. A lion steps out of the archway in front of the hidden walkway (E-S6-a), and GP describes the gem as directly behind a lion.

Every hazard cycles at about 2-3 s (dragon sweeps, gong windups, fire vents). That is slow enough to watch one cycle from a safe shelf; the difficulty comes from chaining cycles over consecutive shelves (J-S4-a, J-S7-a).
There are no holes inside floors. All lethal space is the sky beside the walls, and most falls come from knockback (gong waves, dragons per GP), not from short jumps.
Devices handle the big transitions between towers: a rope climb, the lift and two rope swings (P-S3-c, P-S5-a, G-S5-b/c). They are hazard-light rests, with at most one dragon passing.
Gap widths barely grow (2-4 u on most walls). Difficulty rises by adding cycles: crumble, then one wave, then sweeps, then waves plus sweeps, while the shelf module stays the same.
The bonus adds only the moving cloud and the Nitro walls to the main route's hover gaps and horizontal sweeps (P-B-c, O-B-a/b).
geometryTransfer: Teach by fly-over. Show a sweeping hazard (`pendulum` or orbiting `mover`) passing harmlessly behind the playfield in the opening, then gate the first climb with it.

Wall-climb module. Use 2.3 m wide x 1.15 m deep plank `platform`s with 2.3-4.0 m rises and 2.3-5.8 m horizontal spacing. A full jump lands on a 2.3 m shelf; a double jump, or a ledge grab (lips up to about 5.2 m from a full jump), covers 4 m. Use `crumble` for the first wall and static shelves swept by a `pendulum` (2-3 s period) for the second, never both on one wall.

Knockback lane. A gong-style `sentry` sends a pushback wave along a 1.2 m deep ledge every ~3 s. Back the first one with a wall, then put one over a pit, then pair two side by side so the player must wait for both.

Hover gaps become board air. Turn 5-6 u (5.8-6.9 m) hover gaps into full-ollie gaps taken at or above cruise (6.6 m at 12 m/s, up to 12.7 m at full charge), and keep on-foot gaps <= 4.8 crates (5.6 m) unless a launcher is present.
Use lions as `charger`s at the far end of wide floors (>= 6 m deep), so the telegraphed dash can be read and spun. Use one in front of a hidden route as its signpost.
Tower transitions. Use `ropeswing`s between floating islands 7-9 m apart and a `mover` lift as rest beats between hazard walls, with at most one sweep over them.
